previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome, achalasia, and coronary artery disease s/p CABG was admitted for respiratory distress and chest pain identical to prior mast cell crises. She developed symptoms during a GI clinic visit and was transferred from the ED after treatment with IV Benadryl, Solumedrol, and Dilaudid. That night, she experienced stridor and upper airway obstruction, requiring IV epinephrine and transfer to the MICU. Her symptoms resolved with her allergist’s protocol. Workup showed no cardiac ischemia, stable atelectasis on CXR, and a negative urine culture. Pain was managed with transition back to oral methadone and gabapentin. She improved over three days and was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her allergist, ENT, and psychiatrist, continue ciprofloxacin at a reduced dose, and resume all chronic medications.
